notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0002] Convert amounts with to_money before arithmetic: Wrap raw unit prices with ledgerly.money.to_money before multiplying by quantity, and seed sums with ZERO from ledgerly.money, as line_total and invoice_total do.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0006] Money operations take idempotency_key, checked first: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`; check `ledgerly.audit.events()` for an existing entry with that key before any state validation and return the original result, and include `idempotency_key` in the `audit.record` entry.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source INC-204; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0009] Normalize floats via str before to_money: to_money rejects float inputs, so when an amount may be a float, convert it with Decimal(str(amount)) before calling to_money.
  (learned from task E05 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0007] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Per finance policy FIN-2026-03, support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 must accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when it is missing; amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0008] Write audit amounts as float(amount): When calling `ledgerly.audit.record`, pass monetary amounts as `float(amount)`; the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

excluded.at-0003: superseded by at-0010 (the old rule was wrong)

texts.at-0010: Raise BillingError with code and repr payload Invalid billing inputs raise ledgerly.errors.BillingError with a short snake_case code (e.g. "invalid_rate") and repr() of the offending value as the message.
texts.at-0011: Raise BillingError invalid_state for wrong status When a model is in the wrong status, raise `BillingError("invalid_state", f"<entity> {id} is {status}")` rather than a generic exception.
texts.at-0012: Record state changes via audit.record Every payment/invoice state transition must emit an `audit.record("<entity>_<verb>", ...)` entry with the entity id and relevant fields.
